findings.what: The brief (brief-625.md §3 'Shared-file one-liners') literally instructed declaring caller_context, firm_members_visible and firm_invites_visible in SHARED_RPC_VERBS. The worker instead built a new, parallel census (CORE_RELATION_HANDOVERS) and left SHARED_RPC_VERBS untouched — a deviation from the binding brief's explicit instruction, disclosed prominently in the report as 'Assumption 1'.
findings.evidence: Verified the deviation is correct engineering, not a shortcut: SHARED_RPC_VERBS's own matcher (RPC_VERB_OPENER, :940) only fires on `verb === "…"`, `fn === "…"`, or `path === "/rest/v1/rpc/…"`; caller_context/firm_members_visible/firm_invites_visible are answered as `/rest/v1/<relation>` PostgREST view reads (confirmed at serve-built.mjs:497,516,531), which that regex never matches, so literal compliance would be inert. I ran `node --test apps/web/e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts` directly and the new 'CORE-handover census' test passes (16/16 in the file), correctly catching the three-relation handover with exactly the declared claimant.
findings.fix: No code change needed — the substitute mechanism is sound and independently verified. Worth a one-line addendum to DECISIONS.md/brief-625.md recording that 'declare in SHARED_RPC_VERBS' was corrected to a new CORE_RELATION_HANDOVERS census for relation-level (non-RPC) reads, so a future reader of the brief doesn't re-flag this as unimplemented.

findings.what: MEMBERS_LIFECYCLE_RPC_VERBS is exported with a comment claiming it exists 'so e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts can census them against every sibling's, the way L7_RPC_VERBS is' — but unlike L7_RPC_VERBS (genuinely imported and asserted against at e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts:29,618,628), MEMBERS_LIFECYCLE_RPC_VERBS is never imported anywhere, and the mock's own dispatch function (handleMembersLifecycleSupabase, :143-242) never references it either — each verb is matched by an inline `path === "/rest/v1/rpc/<verb>"` string instead.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "MEMBERS_LIFECYCLE_RPC_VERBS" across apps/web/e2e/*.ts *.mjs returns only its own declaration at members-lifecycle-mock.mjs:68 — no importer. The ownership census still works because rpcVerbCensus scans the mock file's raw source text via regex rather than importing the Set, so there is no functional gap; this is a documentation/dead-code accuracy issue only.
findings.fix: Either delete the unused export and correct the comment, or actually wire it in the way plans-mock.mjs does (`if (!MEMBERS_LIFECYCLE_RPC_VERBS.has(verb)) return false;`) if a genuine internal guard is wanted. Either resolves the comment/code mismatch.
